20. ANTENATAL CORTICOSTEROID:

Benefits:

If given within 7 days of preterm birth

• Perinatal and neonatal death
• RDS

If given in planned c section between 37-38+6 weeks

•NICU admission for RDS
•Uncertainty in RDS reduction
• Uncertainty in TTN reduction
• Uncertainty in overall NNU admission

 

 

Risks:

•Hypoglycemia to neonate
•Potential developmental delay

Steroid talk:

Discussion before offering or considering steroid.

•Should involve women in discussion
•Informed decision of women should be there
•It is Gestation related

Discussion should be based on following points

Planned C/S

@ 37 – 39weeks

Reduction in:

  • •RDS
  • •TTN
  • •Overall NNU admission
  • •Short term hypoglycemia
  • •Benefits are unlikely if birth occurs after 7 days.

Rescue course if treatment >7 days

Likely :

  • •Need for respiratory support

Likely :

  • •Birth weight
  • •Head circumference

Length

  • •Neonatal B.P

  • •Dose dependent effects.

 

Recommendations of Steroids:

Before 24 weeks

Discuss

24 – 34+6 weeks where preterm is anticipated

Discuss and offer

35 – 36+6

Consider the balance of risks and benefits

Twins and triplets

Targeted steroid same as singleton

Only targeted used

Diabetes Mellitus

  • •Not a contraindication
  • •Additional insulin and close monitoring
  • •Steroid discussion with women or her carer @ 37 – 38+6 weeks about the risk and benefits, corticosteroids are associated with neonatal hypoglycemia.

Hypertension

  • •Offer after discussion in case of planned early birth
  • •Offer to SGA, FGR babies if birth is expected earlier but inform regarding lack of evidence.

PPROM

  • •Offer if birth is expected to be preterm
  • •Limited evidence to recommend repeat courses, however further courses may reduce need for neonatal respiratory support.

 

 

 

 

Dose and route of Steroids:

Dexamethasone Phosphate, I/M:

24 mg

 

2 doses 4 doses

12 mg 6 mg

24 hours apart 12 hours apart

Betamethasone sodium Phosphate/ Acetate mix, I/M:

24mg total

2 doses

24 hours apart

How long after Administration is a course more effective:

•After 48 hours of dose, Neonatal death is reduced.
•After 24 hours of 1st dose, benefits seen
•Most effective in reducing RDS if birth occurs between 24 hours to 7 days of 2nd dose.

Contraindications of Steroid:

•Systemic infections
•In case of serious concerns, birth should not be delayed to administer steroid.

Repeat Course of Steroids:

•No reduction in serious morbidity or long-term benefits to babies instead risk of low birth weight and reduced length
•Limited evidence to recommend repeat course of steroid.
•Repeat course reduce need for neonatal respiratory support
•Repeat courses should not exceed three.
